newsitem.title: UK: Colombia eyes 30-year dollar bond -FinMin Ocampo.
newsitem.headline: Colombia eyes 30-year dollar bond -FinMin Ocampo.

text.p: Colombia would like to issue a 30-year dollar bond this year, its finance minister said in an interview on Friday.
"We plan to issue a number of smaller issues this year. We want to go to the 30-year market, probably in dollars," Jose Antonio Ocampo told Reuters.
Ocampo was in London to meet investors ahead of a $750 million 10-year global bond due for launch next week. The deal will be issued via U.S. banks Merrill Lynch and J.P. Morgan.
Last year Colombia issued 20-year paper in the U.S. domestic Yankee bond market. It also issued five- and seven-year bonds.
"Spreads on our bonds are now between 50 to 100 basis points less than what they were a year ago," Ocampo said.
"The general feeling is Colombia has indicators which would allow it to go into a higher rating category and have much tighter spreads," he said.
Colombia is rated Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB minus by Standard & Poor's, the low end of their investment grade scales.
The government plans to raise between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion in the international bond markets in 1997, less than originally expected.
In January it introduced an emergency austerity package to curb the country's high fiscal deficit and to slow the inflow of dollars. Lowering foreign debt levels was part of the package.
